title: 辩论：越想要越得不到的东西，该怎么要？
title_en: How do you pursue what pursuit drives away?

questions.question: 在「越想要越得不到的东西该怎么要」这场辩论里，全场最大的共识是什么？
options: 能直接做的是动作和条件，不能直接做的是检查结果
睡眠、幸福这类东西完全无法练习，只能等它自己到来
只要用力的方向找对了，直接把幸福本身当成目标去追求同样可以奏效
关键是放下期待，对结果不再抱有任何具体的目标
questions.explanation: 总结写明共识是「能直接做的是动作和条件，不能直接做的是对结果的检查」。塞利格曼最后也收回一半：练习要直接，打分要放下。「完全无法练习」是被塞利格曼和契克森米哈伊明确反驳的立场。
questions.question_en: In the debate on how to pursue things that recede the harder you chase them, what was the strongest consensus?
options_en: You can directly do the actions and set the conditions, but not directly check or score the outcome
Things like sleep and happiness can't be practiced at all; you can only wait for them
As long as the effort points the right way, aiming straight at happiness itself works just as well
The key is to drop expectations and stop holding any specific goal for the outcome
questions.explanation_en: The summary states the consensus: actions and conditions can be done directly; checking the result cannot. Seligman himself conceded half — practice directly, drop the scoring. "Can't be practiced at all" is the position Seligman and Csikszentmihalyi explicitly rejected.

questions.question: 韦格纳用什么机制解释「越想睡着越睡不着」？
options: 用力会持续消耗有限的意志力储备，等意志力耗尽之后人就会出现明显反弹
越想要越焦虑，焦虑在生理上直接抑制了想要的那种状态
大脑无法处理否定指令，「别想」在执行中被当成了「去想」
用力时多了个查岗的监控者，人一累，它找的失败信号就占满脑子
questions.explanation: 韦格纳的讽刺性加工理论：每次控制心灵都有一个执行者去够目标状态，一个监控者在查是否失败；人累了执行者没力气，监控者照常工作，它找的失败信号就占满了注意。所以他说用力本身不坏，坏在用力时多了一个查岗的。
questions.question_en: What mechanism does Wegner offer for why trying to fall asleep keeps you awake?
options_en: Effort steadily drains a limited reserve of willpower, and once it runs out you rebound noticeably
Wanting it more makes you anxious, and anxiety physiologically suppresses the state you want
The brain can't process negation, so "don't think" gets executed as "think"
Effort adds a background monitor checking for failure; when you're tired, the failure signal it searches for fills your mind
questions.explanation_en: Wegner's ironic process theory: mental control runs an operator reaching for the goal state and a monitor checking for failure. When you're tired the operator weakens but the monitor keeps working, so the failure signal it hunts for takes over attention. Hence his line: effort isn't the problem — the problem is the inspector that comes with it.

questions.question: 弗兰克尔对塞利格曼「每晚写三件好事」的练习做了什么补充？
options: 应该改成写三件让自己害怕的事，用矛盾意向直面恐惧
为感谢那个人去写，和为让自己幸福去写是两回事
这类刻意练习和躺平等待没有本质区别，都绕不开过度反思
写的同时应该给自己当天的幸福感打个分，这样才能持续追踪练习有没有效果
questions.explanation: 弗兰克尔同意方法可以教，但指出为自己幸福而写会让人每晚检查「起效没有」，又回到过度反思；为感谢别人而写，目光落在别人身上，幸福才有空落下。给幸福打分恰恰是辩论里大家都认为要放下的那一步。
questions.question_en: What did Frankl add to Seligman's "write down three good things each night" exercise?
options_en: It should be replaced with writing three things you fear, using paradoxical intention to face them
Writing to thank the person differs from writing to make yourself happy; the arrow must point beyond yourself
Deliberate exercises like this are no different from passively waiting; both fall into hyper-reflection
You should also score that day's happiness while writing, so you can keep tracking whether it works
questions.explanation_en: Frankl agrees methods can be taught, but writing for your own happiness makes you check nightly whether it's working — back into hyper-reflection. Writing to thank someone puts your gaze on them, leaving room for happiness to land. Scoring your happiness is exactly the step the debate agreed to drop.
